title: Natural rational actions and their generic coactions
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be an affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $V$ be a $k$-vector space. All these objects and commutative test algebras have one fixed universe. Put $V_R=R\otimes_k V$ with the scalar extension and induced maps of [def-weil-module-base-change]. A natural rational representation consists of group homomorphisms $\rho_R:G(R)\to\operatorname{Aut}_R(V_R)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, compatible with every $k$-algebra map $\alpha:R\to S$: $(\alpha\otimes1)\rho_R(g)=\rho_S(G(\alpha)g)(\alpha\otimes1)$. Use the affine spectrum/global-sections identification [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to define the generic point $\eta\in G(k[G])$ by the identity of $k[G]=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$, and the point $g_x\in G(R)$ associated to $x:k[G]\to R$ by $\operatorname{Spec}R\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}(x)}\operatorname{Spec}k[G]\simeq G$. Define the generic coaction $c_\rho:V\to V\otimes_k k[G]$ as the composite $v\mapsto1\otimes v\mapsto\rho_{k[G]}(\eta)(1\otimes v)\mapsto\operatorname{swap}(\rho_{k[G]}(\eta)(1\otimes v))$. These are the actual natural-action data, affine points and linear map; no equivalence theorem or coaction law is part of this definition.
